To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the globalisation of whisky tourism has resulted in the commodification of the Scottish distilling experience, which has been met by a communicative rationality backlash in the form of an increased demand for authenticity.
The commodification of leisure and the globalisation of leisure industries is an ongoing and contested process.

The production of whisky tourism in Scotland is a Habermas-inspired struggle between two irreconcialable rationalities: the instrumentalism of globalisation and commodificaiton and the individualism of authenticity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the commodification of the leisure experience and the impact of this on the meaning and purpose for individuals and groups.
the ways in which the commodification of leisure is experienced by consumers and the ways in which consumers respond to commodification through a search for authenticity.
how leisure is experienced and how leisure is produced, in particular how it can be understood as the product of a tension between two irreconcileable rationalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production of authenticity in Scottish whisky and whisky tourism represents a Habermas‐informed struggle for the preservation of the lifeworld and the commodification of leisure.
the search for authenticity in leisure is a search for a lifeworld that has been lost, but is still sought after.
the production of whisky and whisky‐tourism is representative of a globalised, commodified, instrumental rationality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this paper explores the tensions between the commodification and commercialisation of leisure and the desire to locate leisure experiences in an authentic lifeworld that is free from the instrumental rationality of the market.

the production of whisky and the consumption of whisky tourism in Scotland is representative of a struggle between the instrumental rationality of the market and the communicative rationality of the lifeworld.

the commodification and commercialisation of Scottish whisky tourism has led to a search for authenticity, which is expressed in a range of ways, and that the authenticity of the product and the experience is a key factor in the success or failure of the distillery and the product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of whisky as a commodity is inextricably linked to the production of a sense of place and identity in the lifeworld.

the commodification of the Scottishness and authenticity of whisky is a reflection of the struggle between the instrumental rationality of capitalism and the communicative rationality of individuals seeking meaning in their leisure lives.
the commodification of leisure can be seen as a process of the rationalisation of the lifeworld, which in turn leads to the search for authenticity in leisure.
